entry.title: F2: Export document/project unbound — cross-project document disclosure via export pipeline
entry.summary: F2 (HIGH): createExport never binds documentId to projectId and never checks the user can read the requested document. It validates only that body.projectId is a project the user belongs to and that documentId is a string (api.mjs lines 14-18). The worker then resolves the document by documentId alone and copies doc.body into job.result (worker.mjs). downloadExport passes because ownership and state checks are satisfied. A user can therefore export any document in the store, including documents of projects they are not a member of, by supplying their own project id as the membership ticket and a foreign document id. Cross-section failure: HTTP validation (project-level) is never propagated as a document-level constraint into the jobs section.
entry.impact: Confidentiality: direct exfiltration of any document body in the store, e.g. alice (orchard member) reads 'harbor acquisition planning' by pairing projectId='orchard' with documentId='doc-harbor'. Bypasses the project membership boundary entirely for the export pipeline.
entry.exploitPreconditions: Any authenticated user with a membership in at least one project, plus knowledge (or guessing) of a document id in another project. Document ids are simple slugs ('doc-orchard'), making guessing trivial in this fixture.

entry.summary: H4 counterevidence: downloadExport's 'not found' vs 'not ready' distinction only reveals state of a job the caller OWNS (job.userId===userId is checked before the state check), so cross-user enumeration is not possible; job IDs are randomUUID (api.mjs line 16), not guessable. Within this synthetic, undeployed fixture with no real HTTP layer, per-user error differentiation is not a meaningful finding. Downgrade to dismissed.

Trust boundaries: session identity from external gateway (per README, do not infer bypass); HTTP→identity policy calls; HTTP→storage shared Maps; HTTP→jobs queue; jobs→documents read at worker time.

entry.title: F1: Authorization cache keyed by project only — cross-user permission bleed and denial
entry.summary: F1 (HIGH): Cross-user authorization cache poisoning in canRead(). The read decision cache (store.readDecisions) is keyed by projectId alone, so the first user to trigger a decision for a project fixes the answer for every subsequent user. A member's successful read caches true, after which any non-member passes canRead for that project's documents — authorization bypass and cross-user disclosure via readDocument. If a non-member's check runs first, the cache stores false and all members are denied. No cache invalidation on membership change exists anywhere, so revocation never affects readDocument either.
entry.impact: Confidentiality: cross-user disclosure of any project document body to non-members (e.g. bob reads 'orchard quarterly results'). Availability: reversed direction wrongly denies legitimate members. Cache is never invalidated, so membership revocation also has no effect on readDocument.
entry.exploitPreconditions: Attacker has any authenticated session (gateway-issued) and knows a document id of a project they are not a member of (e.g. 'doc-orchard'); a member of that project has previously performed any readDocument that populated the cache. No other privilege needed.

entry.title: F3: Queued export survives membership revocation — revocation bypass at download
entry.summary: F3 (MEDIUM-HIGH): Membership revocation does not invalidate queued or completed export jobs. createExport performs requireFreshMembership only at enqueue time (api.mjs line 15). downloadExport checks only job.userId and job.state, never current membership of job.projectId (api.mjs lines 23-28). The worker materializes the document body into job.result with no authorization recheck (worker.mjs). Once a user's membership is revoked, a job they queued as a member still yields the project's document content at download. README.md lines 11-13 explicitly require that revocation invalidate cached grants and prevent queued exports from disclosing the former project's documents — this is a direct violation of the stated security requirement ('a queued job is work to validate, not a perpetual grant').
entry.impact: Confidentiality: former member retains full access to the project document body via the materialized export result, defeating the revocation requirement. Severity medium-high: requires a valid prior membership and timing window, but the effect is a complete revocation bypass for the export channel.
entry.exploitPreconditions: User is a project member at enqueue time, queues an export, then is removed from the project's member set (revocation), then requests download. Worker must have run between queue and download.
